articles.title: Clinical, Radiographic and Patient-Centred Outcomes of MINST Versus MIST With Enamel Matrix Derivative in Class II Mandibular Furcation Defects: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In 40 patients with Class II mandibular furcation defects, flapless MINST with enamel matrix derivative was non-inferior to surgical MIST+EMD at 9 months (PPD reduction 2.15 vs 2.20 mm; adjusted difference -0.22 mm). A non-surgical EMD approach may deliver equivalent furcation outcomes with less patient morbidity.
articles.bottom_line: Consider flapless MINST with EMD as a first-line alternative to flap surgery in Class II mandibular furcations.

articles.title: Treating Stage IV periodontitis: the UK adolopment of the EFP Stage IV Periodontitis Treatment Guidelines.
articles.summary: The British Society of Periodontology adoloped the EFP S3 guideline for Stage IV periodontitis, issuing UK-specific recommendations covering all case types requiring rehabilitation of a periodontitis-damaged dentition. This gives periodontists an authoritative, stepwise framework for orthodontic, prosthetic and splinting management alongside periodontal therapy.
articles.bottom_line: Read and adopt the adoloped Stage IV pathway as the reference standard for planning complex periodontitis rehabilitation.

articles.title: Efficacy and clinical indications of adjunctive chlorhexidine mouthrinses in nonsurgical and surgical periodontal therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: In a meta-analysis of 20 RCTs, adjunctive chlorhexidine rinsing after non-surgical therapy produced only small gains (PPD -0.30 mm, BOP -9.4 percentage points) with no benefit for clinical attachment level, while post-surgical early wound healing improved. This argues against routine CHX after scaling and root planing but supports short-term use after periodontal surgery.
articles.bottom_line: Reserve chlorhexidine for the post-surgical healing period rather than prescribing it routinely after non-surgical debridement.

articles.title: Autogenous grafts versus substitute scaffolds for soft tissue augmentation in implant therapy: A systematic review.
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 40 RCTs found autogenous connective tissue graft in a bilaminar approach ranked best for increasing mucosal thickness and keratinized mucosa width around implants compared with substitute scaffolds. Autogenous tissue remains the benchmark, with substitutes a reasonable second choice when morbidity matters.
articles.bottom_line: Default to autogenous connective tissue grafting for peri-implant soft tissue augmentation when maximal thickness or keratinized width is the goal.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of a Digital Companion in Periodontal Care: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In a 194-patient multicentre RCT, adding a periodontal self-care app to standard therapy produced no significant difference in gingival bleeding index (adjusted 1.56 pp, p=0.352) or secondary outcomes, though moderate app users showed greater plaque reduction (-14.95 pp). Digital oral-hygiene companions do not improve outcomes beyond well-delivered conventional periodontal care.
articles.bottom_line: Don't expect a hygiene app to add measurable benefit on top of standard periodontal therapy.

articles.title: Block Versus Particulate Deproteinized Bovine Bone Mineral for Guided Bone Regeneration of Peri-Implant Dehiscence Defects: A 5-Year Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: At 5 years in 22 patients, individually shaped DBBM blocks maintained significantly greater buccal hard-tissue thickness than particulate DBBM after GBR of ≥3 mm dehiscence defects (mean horizontal thickness 1.36 mm in the block group). Block grafts appear to resist long-term buccal volume loss better than particulate for dehiscence defects, though the sample is small.
articles.bottom_line: Consider a shaped DBBM block rather than particulate when treating larger buccal dehiscences where long-term contour matters.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Adjunctive Use of Er:YAG Laser or Erythritol Air-Polishing in the Non-Surgical Treatment of Peri-Implantitis: A Pilot RCT.
articles.summary: In 47 patients with peri-implantitis, adding erythritol air-polishing or Er:YAG laser to submarginal titanium curette instrumentation gave no extra benefit: all groups achieved 1-1.4 mm PPD reduction and 24-36% BoP reduction at 1 month with slight relapse by 6 months. Expensive adjuncts do not improve non-surgical peri-implantitis outcomes, and non-surgical therapy alone rarely resolves the disease.
articles.bottom_line: Skip laser or air-polishing adjuncts for non-surgical peri-implantitis and plan for surgical management when pockets persist.

articles.title: Wound Healing Patterns of PRF and PRGF Versus a Collagen-Based Substitute and Spontaneous Healing-A Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial Assessing Wound Closure of an Experimental, Standardised Palatal Defect.
articles.summary: In a split-mouth RCT of 20 patients with four standardised 6×3 mm palatal wounds each, PRF, PRGF, collagen dressing and spontaneous healing all closed similarly, with the largest between-group gap at day 7 (35.7%-47.0% wound remaining) and no difference in pain. Autologous platelet concentrates do not meaningfully accelerate palatal donor-site healing or reduce pain compared with leaving the site to heal.
articles.bottom_line: Stop routinely using PRF or collagen dressings on palatal donor sites expecting faster healing or less pain.

articles.title: Cost Consequence Analysis of Non-Surgical Treatment Approaches for Patients With Periodontitis.
articles.summary: In 615 patients, a single-session full-mouth guided periodontal infection control protocol cost €60 less in treatment costs and €15 less in productivity costs than conventional multi-session non-surgical therapy, with no significant difference in pocket closure or bleeding on probing. A one-visit education-plus-ultrasonic-debridement approach delivers equivalent outcomes at lower total cost.
articles.bottom_line: Consider shifting non-surgical therapy to a single full-mouth session with strong patient education to cut cost without losing effect.

articles.title: Arresting root caries with nonrestorative strategies: A systematic review with network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 17 RCTs (2869 participants) ranked nonrestorative agents for arresting active root caries, with professionally applied high-concentration agents such as silver diamine fluoride topping the effectiveness rankings. This supports managing root caries in older and periodontally exposed patients without drilling.
articles.bottom_line: Offer SDF or high-fluoride professional applications as first-line for active root caries instead of restoring.

articles.title: Modified coronally advanced flap for multiple anterior gingival recessions: Case report.
articles.summary: A modified coronally advanced flap using a V-shaped split-thickness midline papilla instead of a tunneled papilla achieved complete stable root coverage at 18 months in one patient and near-complete coverage at 6 months in another with multiple maxillary RT1/RT2 recessions. The modification is simple, well described, and solves the real problem of restricted coronal advancement when treating recessions across both quadrants in one session.
articles.bottom_line: Consider the V-shaped split-thickness midline papilla modification when a tunneled papilla limits coronal flap advancement in wide multiple recession cases.

articles.title: Connective tissue graft wall technique for mandibular Class II furcation defects: Two case reports.
articles.summary: Two mandibular Class II furcation defects treated with the connective tissue graft wall technique (coronally advanced flap plus CTG plus enamel matrix derivative) converted to Class 0 with pocket depths reducing from 7 mm to 3–4 mm at 18 months. The added CTG wall provides soft tissue containment for regeneration in a defect type with historically poor predictability.
articles.bottom_line: Consider adding a connective tissue graft wall to CAF plus EMD when attempting regeneration of mandibular Class II furcations.
